newsitem.title: JAPAN: Apollo Finance seeks corp rearrangement - Teikoku.
newsitem.headline: Apollo Finance seeks corp rearrangement - Teikoku.

text.p: Apollo Finance, part of the same group as the insolvent Cosmo Credit Union, has applied for corporate rearrangement under the Japanese bankruptcy law with debts totalling about 111 billion yen, private credit research firm Teikoku Databank Ltd said on Wednesday.
The application was made to Tokyo District Court, Teikoku said.
A court spokesman was not immediately available to confirm the report. A company official later declined comment and the firm's lawyer was not immediately available for comment.
Corporate rearrangement means that a company will try to reorganise itself under minimum court supervision, subject to the agreement of creditors.
Apollo Finance was established in February 1988 by Cosmo group firms, banks, and life and damage insurance companies, the research firm said in its report.
It said the firm extended loans aggressively, taking real estate properties as collateral.
However, it accumulated a large amount of bad loans after inflated land prices began to slip in early 1990s, Teikoku said.
